subject: Security exhibit onramp: audit rights coverage, pen-test scheduling, and evidence staffing
messages:
From: Sam Cho <sam.cho@luminahealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@luminahealth.com, security@luminahealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify MSA security exhibit — pen test windows & evidence onramp

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the draft security exhibit you sent last week. A few follow-ups from our security and procurement teams before we route this to legal:

- Pen test timing: we need a clearer schedule for notice windows (preferred 14 days) and an option for an emergency pen test with expedited notice. Can you confirm Redwood's preferred cadence and a carveout for emergency testing?
- Evidence onramp: Security wants a short, operational runbook that spells out who will receive SOC 2 artifacts and how long incremental evidence requests will take to fulfill (we typically ask for a 5 business day response SLA).
- Staging access: we need to understand what access level your team expects to provide (VPN, ephemeral accounts, or read-only logs export).

We're preparing the procurement package and would like to include a mutual action plan for the onramp items above. Can your team propose specific language or an example schedule we can use?

Sam
Sam Cho
Senior Security Engineer, Lumina Health

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Clarify MSA security exhibit — pen test windows & evidence onramp

Sam — thanks, and great questions. Looping in Kar (legal) and Marissa (solutions/ops) to propose concrete language and an operational runbook. Quick answers while legal drafts redlines:

- Pen test timing: Redwood's baseline is a 21-calendar-day notice for scheduled penetration tests to allow coordination with on-call and staging. We can agree to 14 days for customers in the Enterprise flow (e.g., Dedicated/Private) if Lumina needs that in the order form; Redwood also supports an "expedited" channel for emergency pen tests (critical vulnerability triage) with 48–72 hour notice and joint planning.
- Evidence onramp: we can commit to a 5-business-day SLA for document-style evidence (SOC 2 reports, configuration summaries) and a 10-business-day SLA for operational artifacts requiring engineering pulls (logs exports, infrastructure diagrams). We will include an exception path for items requiring third-party vendor confirmations.
- Staging access: our standard is ephemeral, scoped accounts with expiry tied to the test window; we prefer read-only exports for logs. Full VPN access is only granted under a signed staging access addendum and for bounded windows.

Marissa — can you attach a short runbook and a proposed timeline matrix? Kar — would you review a sketch of redline language for the exhibit and pen-test appendix?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0193

Sam / Soojin / Marissa — attaching two items: a redline sketch for the security exhibit (redlined_MSA_security-exhibit_v3.docx) and a proposed pen-test matrix (pen_test_matrix_proposal.xlsx). High level legal stance and suggested text below. Please review and flag anything that is a hard stop for Lumina.

Proposed legal language (short form):
- Notice for scheduled penetration tests: "Customer shall provide Redwood with no less than twenty-one (21) calendar days' prior written notice for routine penetration testing. For Enterprise customers (as defined in the Order Form), the parties may agree to a reduced notice period (no less than fourteen (14) calendar days) by specifying such reduced notice in the Order Form."
- Emergency testing: "Where Customer reasonably requests expedited testing due to a critical vulnerability or regulatory requirement, Parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete planning within seventy-two (72) hours of notice; Redwood will prioritize coordination but reserves the right to limit testing scope where production risk is material."
- Evidence response SLAs: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to evidence requests as follows: (i) standard documentary artifacts (SOC 2 reports, policies) — within five (5) business days of request; (ii) operational exports requiring engineering assistance (logs, traces) — within ten (10) business days. For requests requiring third-party vendor action, Redwood will notify Customer and provide an anticipated timeline."
- Staging/access: "Redwood will provide ephemeral, scoped access for testing where feasible and will provide read-only exports for logs. Any request for long-lived VPN or full network access shall be subject to separate written agreement and an approved staging access addendum. Redwood will limit the scope of any such access to the minimal systems required for the agreed test plan."

Operational notes (from Marissa):
- Runbook: Marissa is developing a one-page runbook that maps request types to owners, expected artifacts, and SLAs (we plan to attach as Appendix A).
- Sample schedule: propose a default 21-day calendar notice box on the exhibit with an alternate 14-day checkbox for order forms where Lumina selects Enterprise flow. Emergency/expedited channel will be tracked via our support SLA and coordinated on call.

Open items for Lumina to confirm:
1) Does Procurement require the 14-day baseline (instead of our 21-day) to be the default? If so, we will mark 14 days as the default in the Order Form and keep 21 days as the fallback for self-serve customers.
2) Are there any regulatory constraints (state audits, HIE requirements) that would mandate different windows?
3) Any concerns with the 10-business-day engineering SLA for logs/exports? We can propose a staging pull package if Lumina needs faster turnaround for specific items.

Attachments referenced: redlined_MSA_security-exhibit_v3.docx (word redline), pen_test_matrix_proposal.xlsx (matrix with staging roles and estimated pull times).

— Kar
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Sam / Procurement / SecurityOps — thanks for reviewing. Summarizing the current position, next steps, and responsible owners so we can close this in the procurement packet: 

1) Proposed contract edits (legal): Kar has attached a redline and the three short clauses he proposes for Notice, Emergency Testing, and Evidence SLAs. If Lumina is ok with the 21-day default and selecting 14 days via the Order Form, we can finalize quickly.
2) Operational appendix (runbook): Marissa will deliver Appendix A (one-page runbook) that maps each request type to a named owner at Redwood, expected artifacts, and the SLA buckets (5 business days / 10 business days). ETA: Oct 09.
3) Pen-test logistics: We propose the following default sequencing for scheduled tests —
   - T-minus 21 calendar days: Customer provides test scope and primary point of contact.
   - T-minus 14 calendar days: Redwood confirms staging availability and access method.
   - T-minus 7 calendar days: Final scoping call and rules of engagement.
   - Test window as agreed: Expired ephemeral credentials provided; post-test artifacts delivered as per Appendix A.

We can mark the Order Form to show an alternate 14-day selection for customers on the Enterprise flow (if Procurement confirms preference, we'll flip the checkbox).

Next steps / who does what:
- Procurement (Lumina): confirm default notice period preference (14 vs 21 days) and any regulatory constraints by Oct 11.
- SecurityOps (Lumina): review Appendix A runbook when Marissa shares Oct 09 and flag any missing artifacts.
- Karthik (Redwood): finalize redline and provide final exhibit text by Oct 09 for inclusion in the procurement packet.
- Marissa (Redwood): deliver Appendix A and the pen_test_matrix_proposal.xlsx by Oct 09.

Doc and attachments: redlined_MSA_security-exhibit_v3.docx, pen_test_matrix_proposal.xlsx — also linked here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMSA-EXHIBIT-DRAFT

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps move this across the line.

Best,
